Subject: Questions on PHI handling for async uploads and attachments

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — Spectra's engineering team is reviewing the RFP. A few technical/security clarifications from our side so we can scope the BAA properly: 

- We plan to send batched asynchronous document uploads (scanned forms + PDFs) that contain PHI. Does Redwood store the original file payloads or only tokenized/parsed inputs?
- For attachments that are routed to third-party tools via function-calls (e.g., billing system webhook), how are PHI fields redacted or marked for export in the default configuration?
- What's your retention default for user-uploaded artifacts that contain PHI, and can it be set to automatic deletion at customer request?

Please point us to any artifact or diagram that helps explain data at rest / in transit for this flow. Spectra legal is cc'd and will use your responses for the BAA draft.

Thanks,
Rajiv

Hi Rajiv — quick answers, plus attaching a short overview and dataflow diagram. Happy to set up a technical walk-through if useful.

Short answers:
- Storage: by default Redwood stores the original blob for async uploads in encrypted object storage (AES-256 at rest). We also store derived tokenized inputs used for model inference and optional cached KV entries.
- Exports/function-calls: function-calls are routed via configured webhooks. Outgoing payloads can be configured to include only redacted fields; we provide field-level export controls and an allowlist.
- Retention: default artifact retention is 90 days; customers can configure retention to as low as 0 days (immediate delete on ingest) or to a longer retention with an admin policy. We support on-demand purge APIs and retention locks if required for legal hold.

Attachments: redwood-hipaa-overview.pdf (short PDF), dataflow-diagram.png

Next steps: Rishi (cc) can provide the encryption/KMS details and marissa can coordinate a short call to walk through the BAA scope.

Best,

--

Hi Cindy / Rajiv — answering your items with technical detail below. Short summary first: BYOK + customer-managed keys available in Dedicated/Private; platform-managed keys default for hosted. Full audit logging and export available; private package mirrors hosted features with some operational differences.

1) Key management:
- Hosted: platform-managed keys by default (FIPS 140-2 compliant). Customers may opt into CMK (customer-managed keys) for Dedicated and Private deployments. Keys are stored in cloud KMS (customer tenant or customer's KMS for Private).
- Access controls & logs: all KMS operations (encrypt/decrypt/rotate) generate audit trails stored in the immutable audit store; we can export KMS logs in NDJSON for ingestion into SIEM.

2) Audit logs:
- We provide an access log that records object-level operations (object_id, operation, actor, timestamp, request_ip, request_id). Logs are write-once and retained per contract; default export retention is 1 year but configurable to 7 years for enterprise customers.
- Export: filtered export bundles (S3/HTTPS) can be scheduled via the Console or delivered via secure transfer.

3) On-prem / Private deployment:
- Feature parity: the Private package supports function-calls, KV cache and field-level redaction. Differences: certain managed telemetry and auto-upgrade features are disabled; operator-run upgrade process is provided. We supply a deployment checklist and automated installers for air-gapped installs.

4) Backups & DR:
- Backups: encrypted nightly backups of object stores (AES-256) with optional cross-region replication for Dedicated and Private. Backup encryption keys follow the same KMS model (customer vs platform).
- Copies: backups are stored in customer-dedicated buckets/volumes per contract. For hosted customers we keep limited replicated copies; cross-region replication only if enabled.

Extra notes: we support field-level tokenization (PII/PHI) such that exported payloads can remove or replace specific fields. We also have an on-demand purge API and a certified deletion workflow with attestations.

I've attached the proposed-baa-diff.docx with placeholders where we typically ask for customer preferences on retention and key controls. Happy to review a redline.

--
